For a while, he would keep away from those twins.
However luxurious their blond hair, however enticing their breasts, however magnificent their backsides, however plump and taut those thighs, nothing good came of getting involved with them.

Amazing that he had taken so much punishment without a fatal injury. The cuts had spared him only because the enemy's blades were poorly kept. The burns marked where bullets had grazed him. A little farther either way and they would have been bullet wounds.

だから今日は、上甲板のバラック群の一つにも引っこんで、なるべく双子と会わないようにして過ごすのだ。そのバラックというのは朔屋が先頃からこっそり築き上げた、この船の中でも彼だけの隠れ家である。酒をちょろまかし、食糧もかっぱらってきて、さらには先頃寄港した港で積み荷とこっそり交換したエロ本までも持ちこんである。男の隠れ家としては完璧である。
　サボりがばれて後で懲罰喰らおうとも、今日一日はその天国でのんびり過ごすのだ。
　朔屋がかく決意して、気分はうきうきと、足取りは下っ手くそなスキップで船室を出てみると、
lines.english:
Today, then, he would hole up in one of the shacks on the upper deck and avoid them as much as possible. This particular shack was the private refuge he had lately, secretly established aboard. Stolen liquor, pilfered food, even dirty magazines secretly exchanged for cargo at their last port. A perfect man's hideaway.
Even if he was caught shirking and punished afterward, he would spend today at leisure in that paradise.
With this resolve, a buoyant heart and a thoroughly inept skip, Sakuya left his cabin.

lines.japanese: 「……これ、なんぞね？」
lines.english: “…What's this, then?”

lines.japanese:
部屋の扉の前に落ちたる、一枚の布切れ。
　拾い上げてみればソックスの、多少くたびれてはいたが綺麗に洗ってあり、同じ色だがアルファベットが一文字縫い取りしてある。
　Ｓの字だった。この船の中でこの頭文字を抱く者と言えば───朔屋はきっぱりと、決然と、即座に、ポケットにしまいこんだ。
　辺りを警戒してしまったのは、なにか誤解されないかと恐れたからであるが、そうやって見回していると、通路の先にまた一枚の布切れが。
lines.english:
A scrap of cloth lay before his door.
He picked it up. A sock, somewhat worn but freshly washed. A single letter was embroidered in thread of the same color. S.
And aboard this ship, a person with that initial—firmly, decisively, instantly, Sakuya put it in his pocket.
He looked cautiously around, afraid someone might misunderstand. In doing so he spotted another scrap farther down the passage.

lines.japanese: 「……今度も、なんですよ？」
lines.english: “…And what's this one, then?”

lines.japanese: またソックスであったが、今度はＫの字の縫い取りがあった。この船の中でこの頭文字を抱く者と言えば。
lines.english: Another sock. This one embroidered with a K. And aboard this ship, a person with that initial—

　蒐集家の性というものは恐ろしく、そして哀れなものである。罠と判っていても完遂の為には飛びこまずにはいられない。けれど、と朔屋は逡巡する。最後のパンツはＫのイニシァルが縫い取りされているはずだが、そこでもしやＲとかＴとか記されてあったら、朔屋はその忌まわしい事実の発覚に発狂するだろう。とＲ氏やＴ氏に対して大層失礼な葛藤を繰り返していると───

lines.japanese:

　こっちのアンヨはあぁまいよ～』
lines.english:

lines.english: With a somehow familiar song, a leg now extended from the shack's doorway, ladies and gentlemen. Bare, polished beautifully down to the toes, shining in the morning sun. It swept through the air with a sensuality that made him want to fasten his mouth upon it.

The leg withdrew. Next came a backside. It wore a skirt he seemed to recognize, the hem fluttering, as ever, at the exquisite boundary of seeing and not quite seeing.
Sakuya struggled, wavered, agonized. Somehow he held his ground. With a restraint that nearly gave him a nosebleed, he began inching backward.

The resentment and indignation congealed about Sakuya’s throat, all the dregs of his heart—merely having the spirit of neat whiskey slide down it washed the lot away; and his long sigh of utter contentment seemed to burst not from his mouth so much as from a lid springing open atop his skull, like a whale blowing.
Would any alcohol at all have worked this splendid miracle? Not so, not so: it was because this was fine whiskey. To Sakuya, who in the liquor-starved life aboard the Albatross had once mixed caramel into hair tonic and forced himself drunk on it, the stuff was a liquor to rival some heaven-bestowed sacred spring. But why were the twins treating him to such liquor?

　キサラがぶら下げているボトルがまさにそれである。朔屋の下顎も同様にかくんとぶら下がって落ちそうになって、慌てて嵌[は]めこみ直す。

This unadulterated whiskey tasted remarkably like the bottle he had saved for today's special treat. He had been looking forward to sipping it neat, or giving it a light stir with plain soda and drinking it in great draughts. Remarkably like?
It was the very bottle dangling from Kisara's hand. Sakuya's jaw dropped in much the same fashion. He hurriedly fitted it back into place.

Otters habitually arrange caught fish upon a bank like offerings at a festival; hence the name. Almost everything Sakuya had painstakingly stored had been dragged out. Which otter had done it? No need to say. The pair of golden-headed otters. One spoke without a trace of shame.

lines.english: Was The Ant and the Grasshopper, Sakuya wondered as he wilted, the fable in which the industrious ant lays in food for the winter, only for the idle grasshopper to sneak into its storehouse and gorge himself at will—in short, a lesson in how the diligent get made fools of? Then again, nearly everything Sakuya had hoarded here had itself been filched from the ship’s stores or cargo, so he was in no position to put on the injured party’s face. If anything, he was the one who could hardly complain if the navigators caught him and quite literally strung him up.

lines.japanese: 「いいからいいから。ほら呑んで呑んで」
lines.english: “Never mind, never mind. Here, drink up.”

lines.japanese: また注がれては差し出されるタンブラー、朔屋はほとんど反射的に呑み干した。
lines.english: The tumbler was filled and offered again. Almost by reflex, Sakuya emptied it.

lines.japanese:
「ぷっはー……うンめぇ～～っ！
　ってだからこれ、俺の酒だろ」
lines.english:
“Phaaa… So good!
But that's my liquor, I tell you.”

lines.japanese: 「気にしないのよそんな事は。どっちにしたって呑むつもりだったんでしょ？」
lines.english: “Don't worry about that. You were going to drink it anyway, weren't you?”

lines.japanese: そしてまたお代わり追加、シサムもキサラも中々に酌の手に如才なく、そういえば朔屋が初めて彼女達と出会った夜も、しこたまに呑まされたようなそうでないような。
lines.english: Another refill. Sisam and Kisara were remarkably deft at pouring. Come to think of it, had they not made him drink a staggering quantity on the night he first met them? Or had they?

lines.japanese:
「んぐんぐ……うンめぇ～～っ！
　……でもいい加減酒だけじゃ……。
　つまみとかが必要デスヨそろそろ」
lines.english:
“Glug, glug… So good!
But enough of just drinking…
Time for something to nibble, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「待ってました。そう来なくっちゃ」
lines.english: “Been waiting for that. That's more like it.”

lines.japanese: 受け取った、ねっとりと濃い舌触りのチーズの切片をクラッカーに乗せた前菜の、濃密な香りと味はウイスキイに灼けた舌にまた実によく浸みてくる。
lines.japaneseRuby: 受け取った、ねっとりと濃い舌触りのチーズの切片をクラッカーに乗せた[R前菜^オードブル]の、濃密な香りと味はウイスキイに灼けた舌にまた実によく浸みてくる。
lines.english: They gave him a cracker topped with a slice of cheese, thick and sticky upon the tongue. Its rich aroma and flavor soaked wonderfully into his whiskey-scorched mouth.

lines.japanese:
「おお、有難う。
　……でもこのキャステロのブルーチーズも、
　俺の……」
lines.english:
“Oh, thank you.
But this Castello blue cheese…
is mine too…”

lines.japanese: 「これ、美味しいよねぇ」
lines.english: “Delicious, isn't it?”

lines.japanese:
「あたしたちもこれ、好きなんだ。
　ほら、切り分けたげるから、みんなで食おうよ。他にも色々あるしさ」
lines.english:
“We like it too. Here,
I'll cut it up. Let's all eat. There's plenty more.”

lines.japanese:
「なんかやけに親切じゃないか今日は。
　だけどやっぱり、それもこれも俺の……」
lines.english:
“You're awfully kind today.
But that and this, they're all mine…”

lines.japanese: 「まーまー」
lines.english: “Now, now.”

lines.japanese: 「食べよう、呑もう」
lines.english: “Let's eat. Let's drink.”

lines.japanese:
───かくして、なし崩しに。
　
　
　───酒盛りは始まったのだった。
　
　
　───朝っぱらから。
lines.english:
And so, by imperceptible degrees—
The drinking party began.
First thing in the morning.

lines.japanese:
「んべべべべ……ごくごく。
　はぁ～、朝酒は沁みるのう沁みるのう」
lines.english:
“Nbehbehbeh… Glug, glug. Ahhh.
Morning liquor goes deep, doesn't it? Deep.”

lines.japanese:
喇叭呑みに煽る。朔屋はたくさん煽る。お酒呑む。これでもかと呑む。
　美女と酒と肴の札を揃えられて、これで呑まない朔屋があったとしたなら、そいつは死んだ朔屋である。否、たとえくたばってがちがちに硬直していようとも、酒を唇に垂らせば、高野水銀を鼻に詰められた死者の如く、ぐにゃりと軟化するに違いない。
　とにかくそんな朔屋であるからして、貯め込んだお大事を根こそぎ供出させられていようとも、もう大したこだわりはなくなって、酒に流してしまっていて。
lines.japaneseRuby:
[R喇叭^らっぱ]呑みに煽る。朔屋はたくさん煽る。お酒呑む。これでもかと呑む。
　美女と酒と肴の札を揃えられて、これで呑まない朔屋があったとしたなら、そいつは死んだ朔屋である。否、たとえくたばってがちがちに硬直していようとも、酒を唇に垂らせば、高野水銀を鼻に詰められた死者の如く、ぐにゃりと軟化するに違いない。
　とにかくそんな朔屋であるからして、貯め込んだお大事を根こそぎ供出させられていようとも、もう大したこだわりはなくなって、酒に流してしまっていて。
lines.english:
He drank straight from the bottle. Sakuya drank plenty. Drank liquor. Drank and drank.
With beauties, drink and snacks all laid before him like a winning hand, the only Sakuya who would refuse was a dead Sakuya. No: even dead and stiff, a drop upon his lips would surely soften him, like a corpse with Koya mercury packed into its nose.
Such was Sakuya. However thoroughly he had been made to surrender his treasures, he no longer held much of a grudge. He washed it down with drink.

lines.japanese: 「えっへっへ、あたしはこっちのシェリー開けちゃおう。アモンティリャードの二〇年モノ。あたしは冷えてなくってもいいや」
lines.english: “Heh, heh. I'll open this sherry. Twenty-year-old amontillado. Don't mind if it isn't chilled.”

lines.japanese:
「んお？　また気取った酒を……あれ？
　俺そんなの持ちこんでないよ？」
lines.english:
“Hm? Another fancy drink… Wait.
I didn't bring that in.”

lines.japanese:
「だってこれ、あたしらが持ってきたやつだもの。
　あんたもしかして、ここにある酒と食い物全部、自分が貯めたモノだって思ってた？」
lines.english:
“Because we brought it.
Did you think every drink and every scrap of food here was from your hoard?”

lines.japanese:
「そーいや見覚えのないモノも……。
　なんで？」
lines.english:
“Come to think of it, some doesn't look familiar…
Why?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでもなにも。朔屋にたかるばっかが芸じゃないってね」
lines.english: “Why not? Sponging off Sakuya isn't our only talent.”

lines.japanese: 「だからこのシェリーもそこらのも全部、好きに食べちゃってよ。ほらこんなのどう、キプロス島の海胆の塩漬け」
lines.japaneseRuby: 「だからこのシェリーもそこらのも全部、好きに食べちゃってよ。ほらこんなのどう、キプロス島の[R海胆^ウニ]の塩漬け」
lines.english: “So help yourself to the sherry and everything else. How about this? Salted sea urchin from Cyprus.”

lines.japanese:
揃って両腕を大きく開いて、惜しげもなく振る舞う笑顔と酒と肴と、その快活な振るまい、親しげな笑顔のなんとも素敵で、山頂にてかの聖者に世界を与えようとした悪魔の誘惑なんぞは、丁重にＮｏＴｈａｎｋｙｏｕで追い返しただろうが、これには抗[あらが]いがたい。
　時にどうしようもなく悪辣で、また阿婆擦れもいいところの双子だが、姐御肌の気っ風の良さも確かにあって、一度酒を共にすると決めて胸襟を開いた双子の背から、さっと清涼な風が吹き抜けるよう、身を任せるその心地好さ、恐らく朔屋が信天翁号に乗りこんでから、もっとも幸福な瞬間であったろう。
lines.japaneseRuby:
揃って両腕を大きく開いて、惜しげもなく振る舞う笑顔と酒と肴と、その快活な振るまい、親しげな笑顔のなんとも素敵で、山頂にてかの聖者に世界を与えようとした悪魔の誘惑なんぞは、丁重にＮｏＴｈａｎｋｙｏｕで追い返しただろうが、これには抗[あらが]いがたい。
　時にどうしようもなく[R悪辣^あくらつ]で、また[R阿婆擦^あばず]れもいいところの双子だが、姐御肌の気っ風の良さも確かにあって、一度酒を共にすると決めて[R胸襟^きょうきん]を開いた双子の背から、さっと清涼な風が吹き抜けるよう、身を任せるその心地好さ、恐らく朔屋が信天翁号に乗りこんでから、もっとも幸福な瞬間であったろう。
lines.english:
Both spread their arms wide, lavish with smiles, liquor and food, their cheerful manner and friendly smiles so lovely. Sakuya would have sent away the devil who offered the saint the world upon a mountaintop with a polite No Thank You—but this was irresistible. Sometimes the twins were hopelessly malicious,
and thoroughly wanton, yet they also possessed the generous spirit of big sisters; once they decided to drink with him and opened their hearts, it was as though a cool, clean wind swept past from behind them. How good it felt to let himself be carried upon it. Probably Sakuya's happiest moment since boarding the Albatross.

lines.japanese: 「海胆とはまたオツな。下手な生より、塩利かせたやつのほうが甘いんだよな」
lines.japaneseRuby: 「[R海胆^ウニ]とはまたオツな。下手な生より、塩利かせたやつのほうが甘いんだよな」
lines.english: “Sea urchin. A fine choice. Properly salted, it's sweeter than mediocre fresh stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなら俺は、お返しにポルフディオ・アネホと台湾産天然のカラスミだぁ」
lines.english: “Then I'll answer with Porfidio Añejo and Taiwanese bottarga from wild-caught fish!”

lines.japanese: 「テキーラとカラスミときたか……こっちゃイイ感じに塩が抜けるね」
lines.english: “Tequila and bottarga, eh… That takes the saltiness off nicely.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ魚揃いで、蒸しホウボウにライムを搾[しぼ]ろう。日本酒もあるよ、貴醸酒だからちょっと甘いか」
lines.english: “Keeping it fishy, let's squeeze lime over steamed gurnard. There's sake too. It's kijoshu, so maybe a little sweet.”

lines.japanese: 「いい、いい、ポン酒は辛口に尽きるとか抜かす了見の狭い奴は塩でも舐めてろ、甘いのだって大好きだごくごくごく」
lines.english: “Fine, fine. Narrow-minded fools who say sake has to be dry can lick salt. Love the sweet stuff too, glug, glug, glug.”

lines.japanese:
「でもシェリーと味醂は似てるよね。
　よく言われることだけど」
lines.english:
“Still, sherry and mirin taste alike.
People often say so.”

lines.japanese:
この日朔屋達が持ち寄った肴は、船暮らしのせいでかほとんどが瓶詰め缶詰めのモノばかり、それでもその種類の豊富なこと、保存食なりの利点を生かして風味にしたもの、料亭やビストロの出来たてとは異なる質ながら美味佳肴ばかりで。
　朔屋もシサムもキサラもよく大いに喰らいかつ呑んだ。
lines.japaneseRuby:
この日朔屋達が持ち寄った肴は、船暮らしのせいでかほとんどが瓶詰め缶詰めのモノばかり、それでもその種類の豊富なこと、保存食なりの利点を生かして風味にしたもの、料亭やビストロの出来たてとは異なる質ながら[R美味佳肴^びみかこう]ばかりで。
　朔屋もシサムもキサラもよく大いに喰らいかつ呑んだ。
lines.english:
Perhaps because of life aboard, nearly everything they had brought was bottled or canned. Yet what variety! Food that turned the advantages of preservation into flavor. Different from fresh dishes at a fine Japanese restaurant or a bistro, but all delicious.
Sakuya, Sisam and Kisara ate heartily and drank mightily.

lines.japanese:
「しかし───俺は絶対またなんかの罠かと思ったんだよな、正直なところ。
　だってあんた達、いつも色仕掛けで俺を釣るし」
lines.english:
“Still… Honestly, I was sure it was another trap.
You're always using your charms to reel me in.”

lines.japanese: 「あっはっは、なら色仕掛けもない不意打ち闇討ちの方がいい？」
lines.english: “Ha, ha, ha. Would you prefer an ambush in the dark with no charms involved?”

lines.japanese: とかなんとか、ちらちら太腿を見せながら。
lines.japaneseRuby: とかなんとか、ちらちら[R太腿^ふともも]を見せながら。
lines.english: She said it with little flashes of thigh.

lines.japanese: 「いやそんなの御免蒙[こうむ]る。見れるだけでもいい。見るだけでなくって、触れたり舐めたりできればもっと幸せだ。ヤれたりできたら愚息も昇天」
lines.english: “No, thank you. Looking's enough. Better still if I could touch and lick instead of just looking. And if we did it, my little lad would ascend to heaven.”

lines.japanese:
「そのネタはもういいっての。
　でもホント、判りやすいよね朔屋って。
　下半身に正直すぎる」
lines.english:
“Enough of that joke.
But you really are easy to read, Sakuya.
Too honest with the lower half.”

lines.japanese: 「おうとも、硬派とクールを気取って、そんで女の方からあんよ開いてくれる様な美形じゃないってことなんて、俺判ってるもんちゃんと」
lines.english: “Of course. I know perfectly well I'm not handsome enough to play tough and cool and have women open their legs for me.”

lines.japanese: 「それにだって、楽しいもん、女の子と遊んでると。それを考えると、罠だ仕掛けだって見えても、つい行っちゃうもん。アハハははは、信じた俺が莫迦でしたーぁぁ、ああん」
lines.english: “And it's fun, playing with women. Thinking of that, even if I can see a trap, a setup, I go anyway. Ahahahahaha! I was a fool to believe yooou… Ahhh.”

lines.japanese:
卵黄で練り合わせた小海老の擂り身をクラッカーで挟んだ奴をばりばり咬みながら、朔屋は右の眉と目を笑いの三日月にして、左に泣きの涙を滲ませる、一人福笑いという、無駄に小器用な真似をこなして、食って笑って泣いてと忙しい。
　その上言っている事も、こうあけすけに過ぎては気取らず飾らずの粋[いき]に通ずるどころか、莫迦を晒す恥を知らないというだけだこれでは。こらえかねたか、胡座から股割りの前にのめって、すまん寝の様[ざま]、俯けた顔の下から漏れ出すのは嘆きか笑いか、声がくぐもり混ざって聞き苦しい。
lines.japaneseRuby:
卵黄で練り合わせた[R小海老^シュリンプ]の擂り身をクラッカーで挟んだ奴をばりばり咬みながら、朔屋は右の眉と目を笑いの三日月にして、左に泣きの涙を滲ませる、一人福笑いという、無駄に小器用な真似をこなして、食って笑って泣いてと忙しい。
　その上言っている事も、こうあけすけに過ぎては気取らず飾らずの粋[いき]に通ずるどころか、莫迦を晒す恥を知らないというだけだこれでは。こらえかねたか、[R胡座^あぐら]から股割りの前にのめって、すまん寝の様[ざま]、[R俯^うつむ]けた顔の下から漏れ出すのは嘆きか笑いか、声がくぐもり混ざって聞き苦しい。
lines.english:
Crunching crackers filled with shrimp paste kneaded with egg yolk, Sakuya shaped his right eye and eyebrow into crescents of laughter while tears welled on the left—a one-man funny-face puzzle, a pointless little feat of dexterity, busy eating, laughing, crying.
With candor this naked, there was no question of unpretentious charm: only a fool too shameless to know he was making a spectacle of himself. Unable to bear it, perhaps, he pitched forward from his cross-legged seat, legs splayed wide, like a cat sleeping with its face pressed down; laughter or lament escaped from beneath that lowered face, muffled together into an unpleasant sound.

lines.japanese:
いい大人の本音というのはさっきシサムがするりと啜[すす]った、酢漬けのチベル川鰈の切り身といった珍味の類と同じで、小出しにするから有り難みがあるのであり、遠慮もなく垂れ流しにされては胸焼けがする。
　がシサムにはあまりに哀れの度合いが過ぎて胸に迫ったと見えて、乳房の中に抱き寄せ聖母のように甘えさせてやりたげに、物優しい眼差しで、朔屋に差し延べようとした手は、キサラに横から叩[はた]き落とされた。
lines.english:
An adult's true feelings are like the delicacy Sisam had just smoothly swallowed—a piece of pickled flounder from the Tiber. Valued because served in little portions. Pour them out without restraint and they give you heartburn.
Yet his excessive pitifulness seemed to move Sisam. With gentle eyes, as though she wished to gather him into her breasts like the Virgin and let him be indulged, she reached a hand toward him. Kisara knocked it down from the side.

lines.japanese: 駄目、駄目と無言で首を振って片割れの軽挙を戒める。そんな仏心を見せたら、抱擁だけで済むはずがないと、大怪魚悪婁の一件での経験からの忠告に、シサムも憑きモノが落ちたかの目覚め顔、厄落としと杯の薬草リキュール酒を呑み干した。
lines.japaneseRuby: 駄目、駄目と無言で首を振って片割れの軽挙を戒める。そんな仏心を見せたら、抱擁だけで済むはずがないと、大怪魚[R悪婁^アクル]の一件での経験からの忠告に、シサムも憑きモノが落ちたかの目覚め顔、厄落としと杯の薬草リキュール酒を呑み干した。
lines.english: No, no, she shook her head silently, warning her other half against rashness. Show such mercy and he would not stop at an embrace. Advice born of the affair with the monstrous fish Akuru. Sisam seemed to wake as though a spirit had left her. To dispel the ill luck, she emptied her cup of herbal liqueur.

lines.japanese: 「泣いてんだか笑ってるんだか、どっちかにしようよ。まあ、今日だって確かに胸とお尻で釣ったけど、後でなんかを吹っかけるつもりはないって」
lines.english: “Laughing or crying, pick one. Well, yes, today we did lure you with boobs and bottoms. But we're not setting you up for something afterward.”

lines.japanese:
「単に朔屋と酒呑みたかっただけ。
　あんたが来てからこういう機会、考えてみればなかったし」
lines.english:
“Just wanted to drink with you.
Come to think of it, we haven't had a chance like this since you came aboard.”

lines.japanese: それに、こないだの偽幽霊の時は、あんたも一応頑張ったしね、の労[ねぎら]いが小声だったのは、この二人にして照れがあったのかも知れない。信じられないことだが。
lines.english: “Besides, you did your bit when those fake ghosts came around,” they added under their breath. Perhaps even these two were capable of embarrassment when it came to offering praise. Incredible though that was.

lines.japanese: 「あの智里とは、ちょくちょく隠れ酒してるみたいだけどね───あ、もしかしてあいつも呼んだ方がよかった？」
lines.english: “You seem to sneak drinks with that Tomosato fairly often. Ah, should we have invited him too?”

lines.japanese: 「らろーーーっ、らめええええ、智里きたら女の子とか、きっとあんたらも、あいつの方に行っちゃうの……だってあいつのほうが絶対もてるし」
lines.english: “Nooooo! Don't! Tomosato comes, all the women, even you two, you'll go to him… He definitely gets more women than me.”

lines.japanese: 「こ、ここだけの話ですが姐さん、智里って、女の子と来たら女衒に売り飛ばしたり岡場所に追いやったりちょっと素敵なお風呂に沈めたりするヤツですぜ？」
lines.japaneseRuby: 「こ、ここだけの話ですが姐さん、智里って、女の子と来たら[R女衒^ぜげん]に売り飛ばしたり岡場所に追いやったりちょっと素敵なお風呂に沈めたりするヤツですぜ？」
lines.english: “J-just between us, Sis, Tomosato's the sort who sells women to procurers, sends them to unlicensed brothels, dumps them in one of those nice bathhouses, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「食い物にされた女は数知れず、みんなが泣いてその涙がこの海にどんだけ流れこんでいる事やら知れたもんじゃないのホントに」
lines.english: “No counting the women he's preyed on. All weeping. No telling how many of their tears have run into this sea. Honestly.”

lines.japanese: 岡っ引きに告げ口する町奴か、片手を屏風と立てて耳打ちしようとて、ついでに耳たぶの匂いでも嗅ごうとしてきた朔屋のこめかみを鉄の爪で掴んで押し遣りながら、シサム、
lines.english: Like a townsman tattling to a constable, he raised a hand as a screen to whisper—and tried to sniff her earlobe while he was at it. Sisam caught his temple in an iron claw and pushed him away.

lines.japanese: 「……呑み友達つかまえて、ようも臆面なくあることないこと」
lines.english: “…Some drinking buddy you are. Mixing truth and lies without a blush.”

lines.japanese: 「もしかして朔屋、本当はあれのこと、嫌ってるとか？」
lines.english: “Sakuya, do you actually hate him?”

lines.japanese: 「ばーははははっはは、嫌うも何もあーた、あいつぁ殺し屋ですよこ・ろ・ち・や。しかもターゲットは俺だっていう。酒でも呑まにゃあ正気で話せませんわい」
lines.english: “Bahahahaha! Hate him? He's an assassin, my dear. An ash-shash-in. And says I'm his target. Can't talk to him sober without losing my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「……それ、言ってること完全に破綻してるけど、確かにすっかり忘れてたわ……あれが殺し屋だってこと」
lines.english: “…That's completely incoherent. But I really had forgotten… that he's an assassin.”

lines.japanese: 「そういやそうだっけ……。やっぱおかしいわ、あいつもあんたも」
lines.english: “Oh, right, he is… You and he are both strange.”

lines.english: “That was the idea. But he's been the one making us laugh, hasn't he?”

lines.japanese: 本当に可笑しい奴だと、二人は酔い果てた朔屋に向けて、改めて乾杯して、向き合って腕絡めて、互いの酒を互いの口に流しこんで、さも愉快そうな、そして満悦の吐息をついた事である。
lines.english: What a funny man he was. They toasted the thoroughly sodden Sakuya again, then faced each other, linked arms and poured their drinks into each other's mouths. How delighted they looked. They sighed in complete contentment.
